chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: The Biddle marching band under T. B. Jones
summary: At Biddle he played in a 25-30 piece marching band; his improvised turn-back lines annoyed director T. B. Jones.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, when you went to college, did you continue to study music?
yeah, I continued to study. I was in the band there, in the band there in Biddle. A fellow by the name of T. B. Jones had charge of the band. Yes.
And was this a concert band or a marching band, or --
Yeah, this was a marching band. He played marches. I was young and flowery -- you know how youngsters are.
And I played, and he'd give the signal for to go -- (unintelligible) and I'd go ta-ta-ta-ta- -- and kept going and it made him sore. I don't blame him.
In other words, you would improvise a little something at the end or --
I was giving that repetition to -- we call it turn back --
To turn back or turn around, one of those things. And that threw the band and the band heard the

lead so strong and they went back and when they kept playing it, all right, then he just stood up and he played and he played I wanted to take down/ and (unintelligible) he made me play, so I didn't do that any more.
He was shooting you through the grease, as they say.
How big a band was this at Biddle?
At Biddle? Oh, as near as I can think it was around about 25 or 30 musicians in there.
Pretty good size band. Pretty good size band it was.
